blocks.text: Inside its PID namespace your app is PID 1, and the kernel gives PID 1 two duties most apps don't handle: signals with default disposition are ignored unless a handler is installed, and orphaned children must be reaped.
`docker stop` sends SIGTERM; a PID 1 without a handler ignores it; after 10 s Docker sends SIGKILL. Result: slow stops, exit 137, no graceful draining.
Orphans are re-parented to PID 1. If PID 1 never calls `wait()`, exited children stay as zombies until the pids limit blocks new forks (common with subprocess-heavy workers, headless Chrome, ffmpeg).

blocks.code:
CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0          # PID 1 = /bin/sh; SIGTERM never reaches uvicorn
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]   # exec form: uvicorn is PID 1

#!/bin/sh
set -e
python -m app.check_config
exec "$@"        # replace the shell so the app becomes PID 1

items: uvicorn, gunicorn, nginx and Postgres install SIGTERM handlers and behave correctly as PID 1.
Your own Python scripts don't: Python only maps SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt.

blocks.text: Q: "What's the PID 1 problem?" A: "PID 1 ignores signals it has no handler for and must reap zombies. Shell-form CMD or an entrypoint without exec makes sh PID 1, which swallows SIGTERM. Fix it with exec form, `exec "$@"`, and an init such as tini when children are spawned."

items: Add tini when the app spawns subprocesses.
